input.command:
mkdir -p spec/ui/animations/rise-in src/animations && cat > spec/ui/animations/rise-in/index.pi <<'EOF'
use /lib

export scope RiseInAnimation:
    concept: {RiseInAnimationConcept}

concept RiseInAnimationConcept:
    pitch:
        How something that floats over the window, holding the user's attention
        while it's there, comes in and goes away: rising gently into place over
        a dimming window, and sinking away again. Anything shown that way can
        use it.

    shape: {RiseInAnimationShape}

shape RiseInAnimationShape:
    description:
        Two parts move together: the surface, which is whatever comes in, and
        the dimming, which darkens everything behind it. Both follow one quick
        spring that settles in about a quarter of a second, from gone to fully
        in when coming in, and back when going away. Only how they look moves:
        where the surface settles, and so where it takes the mouse and focus,
        is its place from the start.

    comingIn:
        The dimming darkens the window behind from not at all to 40% black. The
        surface fades in from transparent as it rises into place from about 28
        pixels below, easing to a stop, as though tipping up towards the
        viewer. It comes in afresh each time what uses it opens.

    goingAway:
        The same played backwards: the surface fades out as it sinks the same
        distance, and the dimming fades away. While it goes, neither takes the
        mouse nor focus, so what is beneath can be used straight away, and
        something opened meanwhile comes in as usual. Once the spring has had
        about a quarter of a second, it's gone.

    swapping:
        Changing what the surface holds while it's in swaps it in place without
        animating: only coming in and going away animate.
EOF
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='/home/hyphyphyph/piton/repl/spec/ui/components/inset-panel/index.pi'; s=open(p).read()
i=s.index("    animating:\n"); j=s.index("    modal:\n")
s=s[:i]+"""    animating:
        The panel comes in each time it opens and goes away each time it closes
        with the @{RiseInAnimation}: the panel is its surface, and the dimmed
        window around the panel is its dimming. Switching what the panel holds,
        such as opening a diff while the settings are open, swaps it in place.

"""+s[j:]
s=s.replace("use /lib\n","use /lib\nfrom /ui/animations/rise-in import RiseInAnimation\n",1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

content.text:
The inset panel's animation is now its own reusable piece, `RiseInAnimation`, in both the spec and the code, and the inset panel refers to it. All tests pass (173, 1 ignored).

**Spec:** the new `spec/ui/animations/rise-in/index.pi` describes the whole animation without reference to panels. It covers:
- **Parts:** the surface (whatever comes in) and the dimming behind it, both on one quick spring of about a quarter second. Only how they look moves, never where they take clicks or focus.
- **Coming in:** the dim darkens to 40% black while the surface fades in and rises about 28px into place.
- **Going away:** the same in reverse. While it goes, neither part blocks the mouse or holds focus, and something opened meanwhile comes in as usual.
- **Swapping:** changing what the surface holds doesn't animate.

The inset panel spec's `animating` section now just says the panel uses `@{RiseInAnimation}`, with the panel as the surface and the dimmed window as the dimming.

**Code:** the new `src/animations/rise_in.rs` has three pieces:
- `surface(...)` makes any element rise in or sink away.
- `dimming(...)` is the full-size dim layer.
- `Leaving<T>` tracks what's shown between frames: it counts each coming in and going away, and holds the old content until it has finished leaving.

`src/inset_panel.rs` and `src/main_window.rs` now use these instead of their own copies. Anything else can use them the same way: wrap its surface, add the dimming, and keep a `Leaving`.

**Tests:** a new unit test for `Leaving` checks:
- showing something counts as coming in, and swapping contents doesn't count as going away;
- closing keeps the old content until the leave time is up;
- opening something again cuts the leaving short.

The settings panel animation test from last time passes unchanged against the new module.

`piton check`, `piton build check` and `piton build` ran cleanly, the new `RiseInAnimation.md` reference was generated, and the app builds with no warnings.

- `surface(...)` makes any element rise in or sink away.
- `dimming(...)` is the full-size dim layer.
- `Leaving<T>` tracks what's shown between frames: it counts each coming in and going away, and holds the old content until it has finished leaving.

`src/inset_panel.rs` and `src/main_window.rs` now use these instead of their own copies. Anything else can use them the same way: wrap its surface, add the dimming, and keep a `Leaving`.

**Tests:** a new unit test for `Leaving` checks:
- showing something counts as coming in, and swapping contents doesn't count as going away;
- closing keeps the old content until the leave time is up;
- opening something again cuts the leaving short.

The settings panel animation test from last time passes unchanged against the new module.

`piton check`, `piton build check` and `piton build` ran cleanly, the new `RiseInAnimation.md` reference was generated, and the app builds with no warnings.
